cites.quote: The doctor list (`DOC-2`) shows code, name, specialization, department, fee and status.
The doctor list already has a `Today` column after Status.
A weekly window when a doctor sees patients: weekday, start time, end time
kept for history but not offered for new use
doctor A has an availability block on Saturday and doctor B has blocks only on Friday
Given an Inactive doctor with an availability block on Sunday

findings.suggested_fix: Add an S-2 AC choosing "Sunday" (and one with "Monday") with a non-matching doctor, and an S-1 AC whose doctor works Sunday and Monday expecting "Mon, Sun".
findings.text: Weekday is stored as 1 = Monday. Filter ACs use only Saturday and Friday, which have the same number under ISO and 0 = Sunday coding, so a wrong mapping passes. No AC filters on Sunday, and none puts Sunday with other days in the column order.

cites.quote: lists only the doctors who have `at least one availability block on` that weekday
two availability blocks on Tuesday (one in the morning, one in the afternoon)

findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC: a doctor with two Saturday blocks, filter "Saturday", the doctor is listed once and the total counts them once.
findings.text: No filter AC has a doctor with two blocks on the chosen weekday. A join-based filter (the likeliest wrong implementation) lists that doctor twice and inflates the total, and every S-2/S-3 AC would still pass.

cites.quote: combines with search and the department, specialization and status

findings.suggested_fix: Add an S-3 AC combining "Saturday" with a specialization filter that excludes one Saturday doctor.
findings.text: REQ-7 says Works on combines with search, department, specialization and status. S-3 has ACs for search, department and status, but none for the specialization filter.

cites.quote: open the doctor list with status "Any status"

findings.suggested_fix: Name the status option as the existing DOC-2 filter does, or word it as 'with the status filter not narrowing the list'.
findings.text: S-1 AC4 and S-3 AC3 use the status option label "Any status", which is not in the intent or the ticket. The test could target a label that does not exist.

cites.quote: Given a 21st doctor by name has an availability block on Saturday

findings.suggested_fix: Reword: 'Given 21 doctors have a Saturday block, and other doctors without one sort between them by name, ...'.
findings.text: The S-3 AC4 Given is unclear. 'A 21st doctor by name' does not say that 21 doctors work Saturday, or that doctors who don't work Saturday sit between them by name.

rubric_items.reason: All 15 known REQs are traced, but REQ-7's specialization partition has no acceptance criterion.
Stories are small and mostly one outcome each; S-3 bundles search, filter combination and paging but stays cohesive.
Mostly Given/When/Then and discriminating (no-block doctor, duplicate weekday, count), but filter ACs miss the Sunday coding partition and duplicate rows from multiple blocks on the chosen weekday.
20 per page and 21st doctor are sourced or derived inline; the status option label "Any status" is not found in the intent.
Clear, consistent terms (Works on, Any day, front-desk staff); S-3 AC4 Given is awkwardly worded.
